failure: A node stored `parents` while the walker read `parentIds`. Two nodes fell out of reach and dag_verify still returned ok:true, errors:[].
lesson: A schema field name must never be able to orphan a memory; a DAG verifier must fail closed when the declared count differs from what it reaches.

failure: eval_accept could mint an explicit, confirmed mandate from the mere existence of a mandate.grant receipt.
lesson: Only the owner-signed confirm path may make a mandate explicit or confirmed.

failure: An earlier epoch let any tool call append kind:"mandate.grant" and mint the owner; its first fix refused every grant, so seed-superagent wrote the log directly: two writers and a bypass.
lesson: A mandate.grant leaf is judged by the owner signature it carries, against the pinned owner key, never by who is calling.

failure: Sealed with confidence 0.9: one promotion to the next epoch. Two promotions followed and observe scored surprise 50 on the epoch field, in a log that was not receipt-anchored.
lesson: Predict behaviour, not counters, and seal the prediction in the receipt chain before the act.

failure: Seven DAG nodes and every discovery trajectory verified only against themselves, so a minted node would have passed; the context file had to carry an UNAUTHENTICATED badge.
lesson: A self-consistent memory is not an anchored one: a node is trusted only with a memory.dag.append leaf, and recall says so.

failure: An earlier seed-aura divides reachableDagNodes by Math.max(declaredDagNodes,1). The guard is in the IO collector, not the scorer, so any caller that reaches the scoring path directly gets a defined ratio from zero evidence instead of an error.
lesson: A periphery whose denominator guards convert missing evidence into a defined ratio is worse than one that throws: absence of evidence must surface as incomplete/UNDETERMINED, never as coherence 1.
